findings.verbatim: An infix attached to the stem of an adjective い
findings.issue: しい is not an infix and does not attach to the stem of an い-adjective; it is the word-final adjectival ending itself (嬉しい, 悲しい, 寂しい, 恥ずかしい), typically attached to a nominal/verbal or bound root to form an adjective of subjective feeling. Describing it as an infix inside an existing い-adjective misstates the formation rule.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: しい is a word-final adjectival suffix (接尾語/シク活用の語尾), not an infix: it stands at the end of the derived word and its base is a bound root, noun or verbal element (嬉しい, 悲しい, 恥ずかしい, 騒々しい, 憎らしい), never something inserted inside an already-existing い-adjective. Even in the reduplicated cases where the base happens to be an い-adjective root (弱々しい, 荒々しい), the しい replaces the final い and occupies word-final position, so it is still a suffix, and the productive core cases have no source い-adjective at all. As written, a learner could plausibly derive *高しい from 高い, so the formation rule is genuinely misstated, not merely loosely worded.
findings.correct_fact: しい is a word-final adjective-forming suffix attached to a bound root, noun or verbal base (嬉しい, 悲しい, 騒々しい), yielding an い-adjective of subjective feeling; it is not an infix inserted into an existing い-adjective's stem.
findings.proposed_fix: Describe しい as a word-final adjective-forming suffix that yields い-adjectives expressing subjective/emotional states rather than objectively measurable properties.

findings.verbatim: Without any relation to a preceding event/situation.
findings.issue: This describes 〜にかかわらず ("regardless of / irrespective of"), not 〜にもかかわらず, which marks a concessive/contrary-to-expectation relation; it directly contradicts the contribution's own meaning field ("Although; though; in spite of") and all of its examples.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜にもかかわらず is a concessive marker: the main clause states something that holds contrary to what the preceding fact would lead one to expect (激しい雨にもかかわらず試合は続いた). The reading 'without any relation to a preceding event/situation' is the gloss for 〜にかかわらず／〜に関係なく／〜を問わず (天候にかかわらず出発する), which permits alternative/unspecified antecedents (〜か〜ないかにかかわらず) and carries no contrary-to-expectation implication. While some JJ dictionaries add 「…にもかかわりなく」 as a secondary paraphrase, presenting that as the sole explanation misstates the construction's core function and clashes with the entry's own meaning field and all twelve concessive examples, so a learner would be misinformed and could produce *好きか嫌いかにもかかわらず.
findings.correct_fact: 〜にもかかわらず marks a concessive/contrary-to-expectation relation ('although, in spite of the fact that X, Y'), taking a specific factual antecedent; 'regardless of / irrespective of' is the meaning of 〜にかかわらず (without も).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with an explanation such as "the second clause is contrary to what would be expected from the first".

findings.verbatim: probably not the case that
findings.issue: The pattern 〜のではあるまいか is a rhetorical negative question expressing a tentative positive conjecture ("isn't it perhaps that ~ / I suspect that ~"), as the contribution's own examples show (水不足が続くと…影響が出るのではあるまいかと心配だ = fears that there WILL be an effect). The gloss reverses the polarity and would mislead a learner.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜ではあるまいか is the classical counterpart of 〜ではないだろうか: a rhetorical negative question whose pragmatic force is an affirmative, hedged conjecture ('might it not be that ~ / I suspect that ~'). The contribution's own Japanese gloss (～ないだろうか) and examples confirm this — 影響が出るのではあるまいかと心配だ means the speaker fears the effect WILL occur, and これが普通の状態なのではあるまいか asserts that this probably IS the normal state. The English 'probably not the case that' takes まい in isolation as a bare negative conjecture and drops the interrogative か, thereby reversing the polarity of the whole pattern; a learner would read the examples backwards.
findings.correct_fact: 〜（の）ではあるまいか means 'isn't it perhaps that ~? / I rather suspect that ~' — a rhetorical negative question conveying a tentative AFFIRMATIVE conjecture, equivalent to 〜のではないだろうか, not a negative conjecture ('probably not').
findings.proposed_fix: Gloss as "isn't it (perhaps) that ~? / I suspect that ~" rather than a plain negative.

findings.verbatim: Emphatic expression meaning "N1 is realized because there is N2."
findings.issue: The English gloss reverses the relationship and contradicts the Japanese line immediately above it (「N1があるからN2が成立する」): in N1あってのN2 it is N2 that is realized thanks to N1, not N1 thanks to N2.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In the pattern N1＋あっての＋N2 (e.g. 愛あっての結婚生活), the first noun is the indispensable precondition and the second noun is what is thereby made possible — exactly as the Japanese line states, 「N1があるからN2が成立する」. The English line inverts the variables, saying N1 is realized because N2 exists, which directly contradicts the Japanese explanation and the examples (結婚生活 exists thanks to 愛, not 愛 thanks to 結婚生活). There is no alternative labeling convention in the entry that would rescue this, since the structure field itself fixes N as the あって-marked precondition.
findings.correct_fact: In N1あってのN2, N2 is what comes into being/holds thanks to N1; the gloss should read "N2 is realized because there is N1."
findings.proposed_fix: Change to "N2 is realized because there is N1."

findings.verbatim: また、自分のことには使えない。
findings.issue: The blanket restriction "cannot be used about oneself" is contradicted by the contribution's own examples, which describe the speaker's own experience (「ずっと本を読んでいて急に立ち上がったとたん、めまいがしました。」 and 「わたしが「さようなら」と言ったとたん、彼女は泣き出した。」). The real restriction concerns the speaker's own volitional/planned action in the second clause, not first-person reference generally.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: Read literally — and the publisher's own English gloss says exactly "Cannot be used for speaker" — the statement bans first-person reference, yet example (1) 「…立ち上がったとたん、めまいがしました」 and (2) 「わたしが「さようなら」と言ったとたん…」 both take the speaker as subject and are perfectly natural. The genuine constraint on ～たとたん（に） is semantic, not person-based: the main (second) clause must report an unplanned, non-volitional occurrence, so 意志形・つもり・命令・否定 are excluded, which is why 「国へ帰ったとたんに、結婚しようと思います」 fails; a first-person non-volitional event such as めまいがした is fully acceptable. A charitable reading as shorthand for "one's own volitional plans" is undercut by the explicit English rendering, so a learner is misinformed by an internal contradiction.
findings.correct_fact: ～たとたん（に） can freely take a first-person subject as long as the following clause states an unintended, non-volitional event (e.g. 立ち上がったとたん、めまいがしました); the restriction is against volitional/intentional, ～よう/つもり, imperative or negative predicates in the second clause, not against reference to oneself.
findings.proposed_fix: Narrow the restriction to "cannot be used when the following clause is the speaker's own volitional action".

findings.verbatim: may I?
findings.issue: 「疑問詞＋Vたらいいですか」asks for instructions/advice ("what should I do?", "by when should I hand it in?"), not permission; "may I?" corresponds to ～てもいいですか. It also contradicts the contribution's own explanation that the speaker seeks direction from the listener.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In 「疑問詞＋Ｖたらいいですか」the いい evaluates which option is advisable, so the pattern requests instruction or advice — どうしたらいいですか = 'what should I do?', いつまでに出したらいいですか = 'by when should I submit it?'. Permission-seeking is expressed by ～てもいいですか (Vて＋も), where も marks concession ('even if I do X, is it fine?'); without も and with an obligatory interrogative word, no permission reading is available. The publisher's own note 「相手に指示を求める言い方」and the paraphrase with 「疑問詞～ばいいですか」confirm the advice reading, so the gloss 'may I?' is simply an error, not a defensible alternative analysis.
findings.correct_fact: 疑問詞＋Ｖたらいいですか asks for instructions/advice ('what/how/when should I ~?'); permission is asked with Ｖてもいいですか ('may I ~?').
findings.proposed_fix: Change the English gloss to something like "what/how should I ...?".

findings.verbatim: 都合上 (in terms of economics)
findings.issue: The English gloss is misaligned with the Japanese list: 都合上 means "for reasons of convenience / owing to circumstances", not "in terms of economics" (that gloss belongs to 経済上, which the Japanese list includes but the English list skips along with 生活上).
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The Japanese list is 法律上・習慣上・都合上・生活上・経済上・健康上・～の関係上, and the English list drops 生活上 and 経済上, causing the gloss for 経済上 ('in terms of economics') to be attached to 都合上. 都合上 means 'owing to circumstances / for reasons of convenience' (e.g. 都合上、欠席します), and has no economic sense; 経済 is the word meaning 'economy'. This is a straightforward misalignment of glosses, not a defensible alternative reading, and a learner would be misinformed about the meaning of 都合上.
findings.correct_fact: 都合上 means 'owing to circumstances / for reasons of convenience'; 'in terms of economics' is the gloss for 経済上, which the English list omits along with 生活上 ('in terms of daily life').
findings.proposed_fix: Gloss 都合上 as "owing to circumstances/convenience" and add glosses for 生活上 and 経済上 so the two lists align.

findings.verbatim: do something so that
findings.issue: The English gloss corresponds to the purposive ようにする ('act so that ~'), but this contribution's own explanation and all three examples are the manner usage ('as if doing ~ / in the manner of ~', e.g. たたくようにして洗う = wash as if patting), so the gloss contradicts the sense being described.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In all three examples the ように clause is the comparative/manner ように ('as if ~, in the manner of ~'): たたくようにして洗う = 'wash with a patting motion', 押すようにして回す = 'turn it while sort of pressing', 引きずるようにして歩く = 'walk as if dragging (his leg)'. This is the 比況 use of ようだ plus して marking the manner of the main verb, not the purposive/effort ようにする ('make an effort so that ~, arrange things so that ~'), which requires a distinct main clause and no simile reading. English 'so that' can express result/configuration ('arrange them so that they look natural') but cannot render a simile — '*wash it so that you pat it' is not the meaning — so the gloss does point at the wrong construction, as the entry's own explanation (「実際にそうするのではないが、そのような気持ちで」) confirms.
findings.correct_fact: The manner ようにして means 'as if doing ~ / with a ~-like motion, in the manner of ~' (e.g. たたくようにして洗う = 'wash it as though patting it'); 'do something so that' belongs to the purposive ようにする ('make sure to / act so that ~').
findings.proposed_fix: Change the gloss to something like 'as if doing ~; in the manner of doing ~'.

findings.verbatim: １）Something has been decided independ-ent of the person's volition.
findings.issue: This English line contradicts the Japanese note it is supposed to translate (「ある事情や状況から考えて、当然そうなる」= it logically/naturally follows from the circumstances). It instead states the gloss of the other sense (〈決定〉, a decision made independently of the speaker's will), so a learner reading sense 2 is told the wrong meaning.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: This entry is explicitly the 〈結局〉 (logical-conclusion) sense, glossed as 'will end up' and paraphrased 「つまり、そうなる」/「ある事情や状況から考えて、当然そうなる」— a speaker's inference or inevitable outcome (❶ '7 people in total', ❷ 'he therefore wasn't in Tokyo'), which involves no decision at all and is near-synonymous with わけだ. 'Something has been decided independent of the person's volition' is the standard gloss for the separate 〈決定〉 sense of ことになる (e.g. 来月大阪へ転勤することになった), and it cannot be stretched to cover ❶–❷, where nothing is decided. So the English line is a mismatched gloss from the sibling entry, and a learner reading it would take this sense to be about externally made decisions.
findings.correct_fact: ことになる〈結局〉 means 'it (logically/naturally) follows that…, it works out that…, one ends up …' — an inference or inevitable consequence drawn from circumstances (≈わけだ), not a decision made independently of the person's will (that is the separate 〈決定〉 sense).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a translation of the actual note, e.g. "Given the circumstances, it naturally/logically follows that…".

findings.verbatim: 「Aがなかったら、Bは成立しない」「AにはBが絶対に必要だ」
findings.issue: The second clause reverses the dependency stated in the rest of the same explanation (AあってのB = B holds because A exists); it should be 「BにはAが絶対に必要だ」, so the contribution contradicts itself.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In 「AあってのB」 A is the indispensable precondition and B the result, so the necessity statement must be 「BにはAが絶対に必要だ」 (e.g. 合格には努力が必要だ, matching the site's own example 努力あっての合格). The particle には marks the goal/result for which something is required, so 「AにはBが絶対に必要だ」 states that the result is required for the precondition — the exact reverse of the pattern and of the immediately preceding line 「Aがなかったら、Bは成立しない」. There is no alternative parse of には here that rescues it; it is a genuine reversal, not a notational misreading.
findings.correct_fact: For 「AあってのB」, A is the necessary condition for B, so the explanation should read 「BにはAが絶対に必要だ」 (B cannot exist without A), e.g. 合格には努力が絶対に必要だ.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite as 「BにはAが絶対に必要だ」.

findings.verbatim: ❌私は英語が話しかねない
findings.issue: The counter-example illustrating that かねる cannot express ability uses the かねない form, not かねる; 「話しかねない」 is in fact a grammatical sentence of the separate かねない pattern ("might speak"), which the same contribution later insists has a completely different meaning. The ✗-marked sentence should be 「私は英語が話しかねる」.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The section is explicitly teaching 〜かねる, and the ❌-example must therefore be an instance of that pattern: 「私は英語が話しかねる」. As written, 「話しかねない」 belongs to the separate 〜かねない (「〜する可能性がある」) pattern which the same explanation says is 全く意味が違う, so marking it with ❌ in a かねる lesson mislabels a form the learner is elsewhere told is a valid N2 pattern. There is no defensible reading under which 話しかねない illustrates かねる's inability to express 能力; it is a form slip, not an alternative analysis or convention.
findings.correct_fact: The ✗-marked counter-example should read 「私は英語が話しかねる」(ungrammatical, since かねる cannot express lack of ability); 「話しかねない」is a different pattern (〜かねない = 'might well do / there is a risk of doing') and is not the form under discussion.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the incorrect example to ❌私は英語が話しかねる so it tests かねる rather than かねない.

findings.verbatim: すぎで、食べられない
findings.issue: The conjunctive form of 〜すぎる is 〜すぎて, so 「辛すぎで」 is ungrammatical; the same explanation correctly uses 「飲みすぎて」 just above, so this is an internally inconsistent, ungrammatical example a learner could copy.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The te-form of the ichidan verb 過ぎる is 過ぎて, so the causal-conjunctive of 辛すぎる must be 「辛すぎて、食べられない」. 「〜すぎで」 is only defensible where 〜すぎ is an established deverbal noun taking case particle で (食べすぎでお腹が痛い、働きすぎで倒れた); with an i-adjective stem like 辛- there is no such standard noun + で pattern, and the sentence here is clearly intended as the conjunctive form the explanation itself just introduced (「〜すぎて〜」という形もよく使われます) and used correctly in 「飲みすぎて」. Hence this is a て/で typo producing an ungrammatical model sentence, not a legitimate variant.
findings.correct_fact: The conjunctive form is 辛すぎて: 「このカレーは辛すぎて、食べられない」. 〜すぎで is only possible with established nouns in 〜すぎ (e.g. 食べすぎでお腹が痛い), not with adjective stems like 辛-.
findings.proposed_fix: Change 「辛すぎで」 to 「辛すぎて」.

findings.verbatim: 同時進行動作を表す「〜ながら」を「〜つつ」にチェンジすることはできません
findings.issue: This blanket claim is incorrect: 〜つつ does express simultaneous action (e.g. 新聞を読みつつコーヒーを飲む), as the same publisher's other article on 〜つつ（同時進行動作）states; only the register differs (つつ is more written-style).
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜つつ has two standard uses documented in reference grammars (e.g. 日本語文型辞典): 〈同時進行〉「窓の外を眺めつつ、ゆっくりコーヒーを飲んだ」「音楽を聞きつつ勉強する」, and 〈逆接〉usually reinforced as つつも. The claim that simultaneous-action 〜ながら can never be swapped for 〜つつ is therefore a false blanket statement; what actually differs is register (つつ is 書き言葉的/literary) and a mild preference for durative, same-subject actions, not grammaticality. The publisher's own separate entry on 〜つつ（同時進行動作）confirms the internal contradiction, so a learner reading only this note would be misinformed.
findings.correct_fact: 〜つつ does express simultaneous action (新聞を読みつつコーヒーを飲む／考えつつ歩く), functioning like 〜ながら but in a more written/literary register; only the concessive sense is typically marked by つつ(も).
findings.proposed_fix: Restrict the claim, e.g. note that simultaneous 〜ながら can usually be replaced by 〜つつ in written style, with exceptions.

findings.verbatim: 「〜ていく」は「現在→過去」ということですね
findings.issue: Reversed/incorrect statement: this sense is explicitly defined as 現在から未来への継続, and the same paragraph's own example gloss reads 「これからもピアノを続けていくつもりだ【今→未来】」, so 「現在→過去」 is wrong and self-contradictory.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The sentence 「「〜てくる」は「過去→現在」、「〜ていく」は「現在→過去」ということですね」 states the direction of 〜ていく backwards; 〜ていく in this continuative sense projects from the present into the future (現在→未来), which is exactly what the publisher's own meaning field (現在から未来への継続) and the adjacent diagram (これからもピアノを続けていくつもりだ【今→未来】) say. There is no alternative analysis under which 〜ていく points toward the past — that is the domain of 〜てくる. Even if this is merely a typographical slip for 「現在→未来」, the printed statement is factually wrong and directly contradicts the surrounding explanation, so a learner reading it would be misinformed.
findings.correct_fact: 継続の「〜ていく」 expresses movement from the present into the future (現在→未来); it is 「〜てくる」 that expresses 過去→現在.
findings.proposed_fix: Change to 「〜ていく」は「現在→未来」.

findings.verbatim:
【A】カキを食べていない
【B】カキが苦手なんだろう
findings.issue: The explanation defines the template as 「Bだ。Aとみえる」 with B holding the grounds and A holding the conjecture (「B」には理由や根拠が入り、「A」には予想・推量することが入ります), but every worked example labels the grounds as 【A】 and the conjecture as 【B】, reversing its own key. A learner following the labels would misread which clause takes とみえる.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The explanation's key states 「Bだ。Aとみえる」 with B = 理由・根拠 and A = 予想・推量, i.e. the clause carrying とみえる is A; but in every worked analysis the ground clause is labelled 【A】 (カキを食べていない) and the conjecture that actually carries とみえる is labelled 【B】 (カキが苦手なんだろう). This is a genuine internal reversal, not a misread notation or an alternative convention, since the letters are defined explicitly one paragraph earlier and no re-definition is given. Substantively とみえる does attach to the inferred proposition (the conjecture), so the labelling in the examples is semantically right and the template line's letters are the ones that are inconsistent — either way a learner tracking A/B is told the ground clause takes とみえる.
findings.correct_fact: とみえる attaches to the inferred/conjectured proposition, while the preceding clause supplies the evidence; consistently labelled, the pattern is 「Aだ。Bとみえる」 (A = 根拠, B = 推量), matching the examples where 【B】カキが苦手なんだろう is the とみえる clause.
findings.proposed_fix: Swap the 【A】/【B】 labels in the five worked examples so they match the stated 「Bだ。Aとみえる」 definition.

findings.verbatim: ［い形容詞］は「Aくする」になり、［な形容詞］は「Aになる」になります。
findings.issue: The explanation states that na-adjectives take 「Aになる」, but this sense is about causing a change (〜の状態に変化させる); na-adjectives take 「Aにする」(cf. its own structure field 「な形容詞［ーな］＋にする」 and the example 部屋をきれいにしなさい). 「になる」 is the intransitive/spontaneous counterpart, so the rule as written is wrong and self-contradictory.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The grammar point is transitive 「〜にする」(cause a change of state), and the pattern for na-adjectives is 「Aにする」(部屋をきれいにする), exactly as the publisher's own structure field states (な形容詞［ーな］＋にする). Writing 「Aになる」 substitutes the intransitive/spontaneous form (部屋がきれいになる = 'the room becomes clean'), which has a different subject-marking and no agent causing the change. Even if this is a mere typo, it directly contradicts the structure field and the examples, and a learner reading only the explanation would produce ungrammatical/incorrect sentences such as ×部屋をきれいになりなさい.
findings.correct_fact: For the change-of-state 「〜にする」 pattern, i-adjectives take 「Aくする」 (甘くする) and na-adjectives take 「Aにする」 (きれいにする); 「Aになる」 is the intransitive counterpart meaning 'become A', not 'make A'.
findings.proposed_fix: Change 「［な形容詞］は「Aになる」になります」 to 「［な形容詞］は「Aにする」になります」.

findings.verbatim: 「V辞＋に行く」は、日常会話（にちじょうかいわ）でもよく使いますので
findings.issue: The explanation earlier correctly states that the verb goes in the ます形 (「A」には動詞の［ます形］が入り), but here it labels the pattern 「V辞」, i.e. dictionary form, which would give the ungrammatical 食べるに行く; the contribution contradicts itself on the attachment rule.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The purpose construction 「〜に行く」 attaches to the 連用形/ます形 (食べに行く, 見に行く, 買い物しに行く) — every example in the entry confirms this — never to the 辞書形; 「食べるに行く」is ungrammatical in modern Japanese. 「V辞」is the standard shorthand for 辞書形 (as opposed to V-ます/Vます形), so the closing line does contradict the correct rule stated in the first paragraph, and no legitimate alternative analysis licenses dictionary form here (only nouns, e.g. 買い物に行く, take に directly). Even if it originated as a typo, as published it misinforms a learner about the attachment rule.
findings.correct_fact: The purpose pattern is 動詞ます形(連用形)＋に行く (食べに行く, 見に行く); the dictionary form cannot be used (×食べるに行く). Only nouns of action can precede に行く directly (買い物に行く).
findings.proposed_fix: Change 「V辞＋に行く」 to 「Vます形＋に行く」.

findings.verbatim: ②〜みたいに＋動詞・形容詞③〜みたいだ＋名詞
findings.issue: The form list states that a noun is modified by 〜みたいだ, but noun modification requires the adnominal 〜みたいな (as the contribution's own examples 「薬みたいな味がする」 show). This is both a wrong formation rule and an internal contradiction.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: みたいだ inflects like a な-adjective: predicative みたいだ, adverbial みたいに, and adnominal みたいな. Therefore noun modification requires 〜みたいな＋名詞 (as in the contribution's own 「薬みたいな味がする」); 「＊薬みたいだ味」 is ungrammatical. Since item ② correctly gives the inflected adverbial form 〜みたいに, the parallel item ③ is stating a formation rule, not citing a dictionary form, so 「みたいだ＋名詞」 is a genuine error and contradicts example ②/the ⭕️❌ chart in the same explanation.
findings.correct_fact: For noun modification the adnominal form is used: 名詞/普通形＋みたいな＋名詞 (e.g. 薬みたいな味), not みたいだ＋名詞.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the third form to 〜みたいな＋名詞.

findings.verbatim: 「〜を余儀なくさせる」と混乱しやすい文型に「〜を余儀なくさせる」があります。
findings.issue: The sentence says the pattern easily confused with 「〜を余儀なくさせる」 is 「〜を余儀なくさせる」 itself — the second form should be the passive 「〜を余儀なくされる」. As written it is self-contradictory and the following contrast about subjects makes no sense.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The sentence names 「〜を余儀なくさせる」 as the pattern confusable with itself, which is vacuous, and the immediately following contrast (「どちらも…N1の文型として区別して覚えておきましょう」) presupposes two distinct forms. The genuine minimal pair is the causative 〜を余儀なくさせる (cause = subject: 大雨はイベントの中止を余儀なくさせた) versus the passive 〜を余儀なくされる (affected party = subject: 私たちは中止を余儀なくされた). No teaching convention or notation reading makes the identical repetition defensible; a learner is left with no contrast to learn.
findings.correct_fact: The pattern easily confused with 「〜を余儀なくさせる」 (causative, cause as subject) is the passive 「〜を余儀なくされる」, where the person/party forced into the situation is the subject.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the second occurrence to 「〜を余儀なくされる」.

findings.verbatim: 「AにBを見せる」「BにAを見せる」の形で使われ
findings.issue: The two listed patterns contradict each other and the following sentence: if A is the person (as stated in 「A」には人やグループなどを表すものが入ります), then 「BにAを見せる」 reverses the roles and would mean showing the person to the object. The intended variant is presumably 「BをAに見せる」 (word-order inversion), not 「BにAを見せる」.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In 見せる the case marking is fixed: the recipient/viewer takes に and the thing displayed takes を (友達に写真を見せる), and only the surface order is free (写真を友達に見せる). The explanation defines A as the person (「A」には人やグループなどを表すもの) and glosses the pattern as 「AにBが見えるようにする」, so 「BにAを見せる」 marks the person with を and the object with に — the reverse of the actual valency, not a mere word-order variant. This is an internal contradiction in the very sentence, not a defensible alternative analysis or notation the reviewer misread; the intended second form must be 「BをAに見せる」.
findings.correct_fact: With 見せる the viewer/recipient is marked with に and the displayed thing with を; the only legitimate variant is the word-order inversion 「BをAに見せる」, not 「BにAを見せる」.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the second pattern to 「BをAに見せる」.

findings.verbatim: 「〜を通して」は「〜に通じて」にチェンジすることができます😊
findings.issue: The substitute form is given as 「〜に通じて」, but the equivalent pattern is 「〜を通じて」 (as correctly written in the same publisher's period-sense explanation); 「〜に通じて」 with a noun like 山田くん is not this grammar point.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The productive equivalent of 〜を通して in the means/mediation sense is 〜を通じて; the particle must be を because 通じる here is used in the fixed connective 〜を通じて (cf. 山田くんを通じて知り合った). 「〜に通じて」 is not this pattern — 〜に通じる is the intransitive 'lead to / be connected to / be well versed in' use (駅に通じる道, 日本文化に通じている), which cannot substitute in 「山田くんを通して知り合った」. The publisher's own worked examples directly below write ＝山田くんを通じて…, confirming the flagged 「に」 is an error rather than an intended alternative analysis.
findings.correct_fact: The interchangeable form is 「〜を通じて」 (particle を), not 「〜に通じて」; 〜に通じる is a different, intransitive use meaning 'lead to / be conversant with'.
findings.proposed_fix: Change 「〜に通じて」 to 「〜を通じて」.

findings.verbatim: 「〜を通して」は「〜に通じて」にチェンジすることができます
findings.issue: The particle is wrong: 「〜を通して」can be replaced by 「〜を通じて」, not 「〜に通じて」(「〜に通じて」is a different, non-equivalent expression). The rest of the contribution consistently uses 「を通じて」, so this also contradicts the contribution's own examples.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The instrumental/mediative pattern is fixed as 〜を通じて (Nを通じて／Nを通して); 通じる in the 〜に通じる frame means something entirely different — 'be well versed in' (日本の事情に通じている) or 'lead to' (駅に通じる道) — and cannot express means or intermediary. Since the sentence pattern is 「A」は「B」にチェンジすることができます, the quoted replacement form B is unambiguously 「〜に通じて」, an ungrammatical substitute for 「〜を通して」, and it contradicts the contribution's own paired examples (山田くんを通して＝山田くんを通じて). No dialectal, archaic, or pedagogical convention licenses に here; it is a particle error/typo.
findings.correct_fact: 「〜を通して」can be replaced by 「〜を通じて」(を, not に); 「〜に通じる」is a separate expression meaning 'be well versed in' or 'lead/connect to'.
findings.proposed_fix: Change 「〜に通じて」to 「〜を通じて」.

findings.verbatim: 〜向けだ。
findings.issue: In the list of forms of 〜向き, the predicate form is given as 「〜向けだ」, which is the related-but-different pattern 〜向け, not 〜向き; every example in the contribution uses 「〜向きだ」. This contradicts the contribution's own examples and would mislead a learner.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The bracketed list is explicitly headed ［「〜向き」の形］, so the sentence-final predicate form should read 「〜向きだ。」, matching all five examples (若い人向きだ, 子供向きだ, 学生向きだ, 大人向きの, 幼稚園の先生向きではない). 「〜向け」 is a distinct pattern meaning 'aimed at / produced for (a target audience)' rather than 'suited to', and the same explanation itself treats it as a separate, merely 似ている文型 to be reviewed elsewhere — so it cannot be read as an accepted variant of 向き. No teaching convention or notation reading rescues this; it is a plain typo that contradicts the surrounding text and examples.
findings.correct_fact: The predicate form of this pattern is 「〜向きだ」 (e.g. このカレーは子供向きだ); 「〜向けだ」 belongs to the separate 〜向け pattern meaning 'intended/produced for (a target group)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the listed form to 「〜向きだ。」.

findings.verbatim: 受身形を使う場合は「〜思いをさせる」となる
findings.issue: 「〜思いをさせる」is the causative (使役形), not the passive (受身形); the passive would be 「〜思いをさせられる」or the experiencer-focused 「嫌な思いをさせられた」. The grammatical label is wrong and would misinform a learner.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「させる」is unambiguously the 使役形 (causative): 使役 attaches (さ)せる to make someone experience/do something, while 受身形 attaches (ら)れる. 「恥ずかしい思いをさせてごめんね」means 'sorry for making you feel embarrassed' — the speaker is the causer, not the affected subject, which is the opposite of a passive. There is no established teaching convention in which させる is called 受身形; the corresponding passive/causative-passive would be 嫌な思いをさせられた. A learner reading this would systematically mislabel させる as passive.
findings.correct_fact: 「〜思いをさせる」is the causative (使役形), meaning 'to make someone feel ~'; the passive/causative-passive is 「〜思いをさせられる」(e.g. 嫌な思いをさせられた).
findings.proposed_fix: Change 受身形 to 使役形 (causative) in that sentence.

findings.verbatim: 大変だった、辛かったが〜したことで効果や成果が得られて、いい結果になったと言いたい時に使う。
findings.issue: The meaning describes only the affirmative 〜かいあって (effort paid off, good result), which is the opposite of the headword 〜かいもなく (effort was in vain); the contribution's own examples 「父は手術のかいもなく、亡くなってしまった。」 contradict "いい結果になった".
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The record's headword/expression is 〜かいもなく, but the meaning field defines only the affirmative 〜かいあって: 「〜の効果があって/〜のおかげで」and「効果や成果が得られて、いい結果になったと言いたい時に使う」. 〜かいもなく is the negated form (かい 'worth, avail' + もない), meaning the effort brought no result — 'despite ~, it was in vain', as the entry's own examples 「父は手術のかいもなく、亡くなってしまった」and「残業したかいもなく、納期を守れず」show. Even granting that the source page treats both forms together, the explanation as attached to this headword states the opposite polarity, so a learner would be actively misinformed; the structure field likewise lists only かいがあって/がいがある (plus an unrelated あげく line).
findings.correct_fact: 〜かいもなく means the effort/hardship yielded no result — 'despite having done ~, it was to no avail / in vain', with a negative outcome; only 〜かいあって/〜かいがあって means the effort paid off with a good result.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a gloss for 〜かいもなく, e.g. 「〜した効果・成果が得られず、残念な結果になった」.

findings.verbatim: ×箸でご飯を食べます。
findings.issue: This sentence is marked with × as unacceptable, but 「箸でご飯を食べます」 is perfectly natural Japanese; the intended unacceptable form must have been 「×箸によってご飯を食べます」. As printed, a learner is told a correct sentence is wrong.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The bullet 「単に手段の選択を表す場合には使わない」 introduces examples of ungrammatical によって sentences, and the parallel first line 「×毎日、自転車によって学校へ行く」 confirms that pattern; the second line should therefore read 「×箸によってご飯を食べます」. 「箸でご飯を食べます」 with instrumental で is completely standard Japanese (で marking instrument/means), so marking it × misinforms the learner — especially since the same entry states 「〜で」で置き換えが可能, making the printed line self-contradictory. No alternative analysis (colloquialism, regional form, notation convention) makes 箸でご飯を食べます unacceptable.
findings.correct_fact: 「箸でご飯を食べます」 is fully grammatical (instrumental で); the intended unacceptable example is 「×箸によってご飯を食べます」, since によって is not used for simple choice of everyday instrument.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the starred example to 「×箸によってご飯を食べます。」.

findings.verbatim: 〜が一番いい。
findings.issue: The pattern 〜ほど…はない only expresses 'nothing is as ~ as X'; it is not restricted to positive evaluation, and this contribution's own examples (漢字ほど嫌なものはない, 悔しかったことはない) mean X is the worst, contradicting the gloss 〜が一番いい / 'the best'.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜ほど…はない is a comparative-superlative construction meaning '(nothing/no one) is as ~ as X', i.e. X is the most ~ on whatever scale the adjective supplies; the scale can be negative (漢字ほど嫌なものはない, 悔しかったことはない, 緊張するものはない) or positive (幸せ, 便利). Glossing it as 〜が一番いい / 'the best' misstates the semantics and is directly contradicted by the publisher's own examples in the same entry. The neighbouring notes (subjective evaluation, not for objective fact, the エベレスト caution) are fine, so only the 一番いい/'the best' gloss is defective; the accurate teaching gloss is 〜が一番だ/〜が最も…だ.
findings.correct_fact: 〜ほど…はない means 'nothing/no one is as … as X' — X ranks highest on the degree expressed by the predicate, which may be negative (worst, most annoying, most nerve-racking) as well as positive; the correct gloss is 〜が一番だ, not 〜が一番いい/'the best'.
findings.proposed_fix: State the meaning as '〜が一番だ／これ以上〜なものはない' so negative-evaluation uses are covered.

findings.verbatim: 常識的に〜するのが当然だと言う時に使う。
findings.issue: The headword/expression of this contribution is べきではない (negative, "should not"), but the meaning explains the affirmative べきだ ("it is natural/appropriate to do"), so the polarity is reversed relative to the pattern being defined.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The propositional content quoted is a correct gloss of the affirmative 〜べきだ (常識的に当然だ), but it is attached to the headword べきではない, whose meaning is the negation of that: 「〜しない方がいい／〜するのは当然でない・不適切だ」. Nothing in the meaning field (nor the English gloss 'should', nor the structure line V辞書形+べきだ) signals negation, so a learner looking up べきではない is told it means 'should' rather than 'should not'. The only defense available is that the entry is an alias of the publisher's 〜べきだ article, but even under that convention the displayed definition of the negative headword is polarity-reversed and would misinform.
findings.correct_fact: べきではない (=べきじゃない/べきでない) expresses that one ought NOT to do something — 常識的・道義的に〜するのは当然ではない／〜しない方がいい (English 'should not'), the negation of べきだ.
findings.proposed_fix: State that べきではない means it is not appropriate/one should not do something, i.e. the negative of べきだ.

findings.verbatim:
[英訳]
should
findings.issue: The English gloss "should" is the affirmative sense; for べきではない the gloss should be "should not / ought not to", so the polarity is reversed.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The headword/sourceId is べきではない, whose meaning is the prohibitive/negative 「〜するのは当然ではない・〜しない方がいい」 = 'should not / ought not to'; the entry instead glosses it as 「〜した方がいい／〜するのが当然だ」 and 'should', which is the affirmative べきだ sense. This is not a notational shorthand or teaching convention: the whole meaning field, including the Japanese paraphrase, asserts positive obligation for a negative-polarity expression, so a learner would take 行くべきではない as 'should go'. The only defense is that the underlying producer page is titled 〜べきだ, but that explains the origin of the error rather than making the gloss correct for this entry.
findings.correct_fact: べきではない (べきじゃない) is the negative of べきだ and means 'should not / ought not to (do)' — i.e. 〜するのはよくない／〜しない方がいい, not 'should'.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the gloss to "should not / ought not to".

findings.verbatim:
厌烦
腻
厌倦
findings.issue: The Chinese glosses mean "be fed up / bored / weary of", which does not convey the core modern meaning of 〜あぐねる (to do something repeatedly without success, to be stuck / unable to reach a conclusion), and it contradicts the contribution's own explanation (思い通りに進まず…行き詰っている様子). A learner would misread 考えあぐねる as "tired of thinking" rather than "unable to decide after much thought".
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: In modern Japanese 〜あぐねる (連用形＋あぐねる) means 'to do something at length without succeeding / to be stuck, unable to reach a conclusion' — 広辞苑・明鏡 gloss it as 「…しつづけてうまくできないで困る」(攻めあぐねる, 考えあぐねる, 決めあぐねる). The three Chinese glosses 厌烦・腻・厌倦 all express boredom/weariness, i.e. the 「飽きる・嫌になる」 sense, which survives only in the older 倦む(あぐむ) reading and is not the sense operative in the compound pattern this entry teaches. The defensible defence — that the kanji notation 倦ねる licenses 厌倦 — fails here because all three glosses point to boredom and none conveys 行き詰まり, directly contradicting the entry's own explanation and misleading a Chinese-speaking learner into reading 考えあぐねる as 'tired of thinking'.
findings.correct_fact: 〜あぐねる means to do something repeatedly/at length without success — to be stuck or unable to decide (e.g. 考えあぐねる = 'be unable to come to a decision after much thought'); appropriate Chinese glosses would be 迟迟不能…／束手无策／(做…)不顺利, not 厌烦/腻/厌倦.
findings.proposed_fix: Gloss as 想不出办法／一直做不成、陷入僵局 rather than 厌烦/腻/厌倦.

findings.verbatim: 動詞に接続するときはその動作の頻度が著しく高いことを表します
findings.issue: あまりに(も) before a verb expresses an excessive degree/extent of the action or state, not its frequency; a frequency reading only arises incidentally with inherently iterative verbs. The contribution's own verb examples (あまりにも今の現実とかけ離れすぎている / あまりにも似合っている) show degree, not frequency, so the rule contradicts its own data.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: あまりに（も）は動詞に接続する場合も「程度が甚だしい」ことを表す副詞であり、頻度を表す用法はない（例：あまりに驚いて声が出なかった／あまりに疲れて眠ってしまった＝程度）。頻度の高さは「よく」「何度も」「頻繁に」等が担う機能で、あまりにが頻度読みに見えるのは「何度も」等の反復要素や反復性動詞が共起する場合の副次的効果に過ぎない。実際、当該コンテンツ自身の動詞例（あまりにも今の現実とかけ離れすぎている／あまりにも似合っている）はいずれも程度の甚だしさであり、頻度解釈は成立しない。よって説明は学習者を誤導する。
findings.correct_fact: あまりに（も）は形容詞・動詞いずれに接続しても「程度が甚だしすぎる」ことを表す。動詞接続時に動作の頻度の高さを表す用法はない。
findings.proposed_fix: State that with verbs あまりに(も) marks an excessive degree/extent of the action or state (frequency only when the verb itself denotes repetition).

findings.verbatim: また、一人称の場合のみしか使えません。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that 〜がたい can only be used with a first-person experiencer is contradicted by this contribution's own example 「Ａ国の要求は、政府にとっては受け入れがたいものである。」, where the experiencer is 政府 (third person); such third-person 〜がたい sentences (e.g. 彼にとっては受け入れがたい事実だ) are normal Japanese.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜がたい is an evaluative suffix (難い) that freely takes a third-person experiencer, typically marked with にとって or に: 「彼にとっては受け入れがたい事実だ」「彼女には耐えがたい苦痛だった」「彼女にとっては信じがたい話だった」 are all ordinary Japanese, and standard references (e.g. 日本語文型辞典) impose no person restriction, only a semantic one (psychological/evaluative difficulty rather than physical inability). The publisher's own example 「Ａ国の要求は、政府にとっては受け入れがたいものである」 demonstrates exactly the third-person experiencer that the rule forbids, so the blanket statement 「一人称の場合のみしか使えません」 is not a defensible simplification but an internally contradicted overgeneralization. The genuine constraint the publisher was groping for is that the subject cannot be an agent whose future volitional action is being predicted (hence the oddness of ✕あの人はきっと許しがたいよ), which is a different matter from person marking.
findings.correct_fact: 〜がたい is not restricted to a first-person experiencer; third-person experiencers are normal, usually with にとって/に, e.g. 「彼にとっては受け入れがたい事実だ」「彼女には耐えがたい苦痛だった」. The real restriction concerns the evaluative (not physical-ability) nature of the difficulty and the fact that it does not predict another person's volitional act.
findings.proposed_fix: Restate the restriction as 'expresses the speaker's/writer's own evaluation, though a third-party experiencer marked by 〜にとっては is possible' rather than 'first person only'.

findings.verbatim: 後件には否定形が呼応します。
findings.issue: The contribution states as a rule that the following clause must be negative (and its `structure` field likewise fixes 「すら～ない」), yet several of its own examples end in affirmative predicates: 「怒っているところすら可愛い。」and「正直おかしいとすら思っている。」 This is an internal contradiction and also overstates a real tendency as an absolute rule.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: すら (like さえ) is a 取り立て助詞 marking an extreme/minimal case; it is statistically frequent with negative predicates but grammatically compatible with affirmative ones — e.g. 「子供ですら知っている」「専門家ですら間違える」, and the publisher's own 「怒っているところすら可愛い」「おかしいとすら思っている」. Stating 「後件には否定形が呼応します」 as 呼応 (obligatory concord, like しか～ない or 全然) misdescribes a tendency as a syntactic requirement, and the structure field 「名詞＋（助詞）＋すら～ない」 hard-codes that error. Unlike the hedged 「ほとんどの場合」 in the preceding line, this sentence carries no hedge, so a learner would wrongly conclude affirmative すら sentences are ungrammatical.
findings.correct_fact: すら does not require a negative predicate; it marks an extreme/unexpected example and freely occurs with affirmative predicates (子供ですら知っている、専門家ですら間違える), though co-occurrence with negatives is common.
findings.proposed_fix: Soften to a tendency (e.g. 「多くの場合、後件は否定形」) and adjust the structure line to allow affirmative predicates.

findings.verbatim: こちらは既に起きたことにしか使えません。
findings.issue: The claim that どんなに～ても／いくら～ても can only be used for things that have already happened is too strong and inaccurate; both are routinely used with unrealised hypotheticals (e.g. どんなに雨が降っても行きます／いくらお金があっても幸せにはなれない).
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: どんなに～ても／いくら～ても are freely used with unrealised, purely hypothetical antecedents: どんなに雨が降っても明日は出発します／いくら頼まれても引き受けません／いくらお金があっても幸せは買えない. The standard contrast taught is that たとえ marks the clause as counterfactual/hypothetical, while どんなに・いくら (degree/frequency adverbs) are neutral and cover BOTH already-realised facts (どんなに探しても見つからなかった) and unrealised suppositions — not exclusively the former. The restrictive 「～にしか使えません」 therefore states a false constraint and would lead a learner to wrongly reject perfectly ordinary sentences.
findings.correct_fact: どんなに～ても／いくら～ても can be used both for already-realised situations and for unrealised hypotheticals (e.g. どんなに雨が降っても行きます); they are not restricted to things that have already happened. The narrower restriction (hypothetical, not-yet-occurred) applies rather to たとえ.
findings.proposed_fix: Soften to say どんなに／いくら～ても can also describe already-occurring or repeated situations, unlike たとえ～ても which is purely hypothetical.

findings.verbatim: 前件と後件の間には何の因果関係もなく、元々期待もしていなかったという心理を表せるのが特徴です
findings.issue: The claim that there is no causal relation at all between the clauses is contradicted by the contribution's own examples, e.g. 枕を変えたところ、睡眠の質も改善された and 早めに寝るようにしたところ、朝の目覚めが変わった, where the first clause clearly causes the second.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 〜たところ requires only that the first clause be the きっかけ/契機 for the discovery or occurrence stated in the second; it does not exclude a causal link. Standard descriptions (e.g. 日本語文型辞典) allow both mere discovery (警察に問い合わせたところ、財布が届けられていた) and genuine cause-and-effect results (薬を飲んだところ、熱が下がった／お願いしてみたところ、快諾してくれた), and the publisher's own 枕を変えたところ、睡眠の質も改善された and 早めに寝るようにしたところ、朝の目覚めが変わった are plainly causal. Saying 何の因果関係もない as a defining 特徴 would wrongly bar learners from the most common resultative use, so this is not a defensible simplification but a factual overstatement.
findings.correct_fact: 〜たところ marks the preceding action as the trigger/occasion after which a (often newly discovered or unexpected) result is stated; the two clauses may well stand in a cause-effect relation (薬を飲んだところ、熱が下がった). What matters is that the result is presented as newly learned or noteworthy, not that causality be absent.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword to say the speaker did not anticipate the result, rather than that no causal relation exists.

findings.verbatim:
逆接を表します。
後件には予想や期待に反した内容が述べられます。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that the second clause must contradict expectation is violated by several of its own examples, e.g. 先生に相談したところ、親身になって話を聞いてくれた。 and お土産を買って行ったところ、…とても喜んでくれた。, which are simply favourable results, not adversative.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「〜たところ」as a conjunctive is a neutral 発見・結果 construction (≒「〜たら」): the main clause states what became known or what happened as a consequence of the preceding action, and it carries no requirement of counter-expectation. Adversativity belongs to the distinct form「〜たところが」(and the conjunction「ところが」), and the publisher has projected that property onto plain「〜たところ」, even equating it with「〜のに」. Its own examples confirm the mismatch: 「先生に相談したところ、親身になって話を聞いてくれた」and「お土産を買って行ったところ、とても喜んでくれた」are straightforward favourable outcomes, and 「〜のに」could not replace ところ there without changing the meaning to nonsense.
findings.correct_fact: 「動詞た形＋ところ」merely presents the result/discovery following an action (similar to「〜たら」, formal register); the result may be expected, favourable, or unexpected. Only「〜たところが」/接続詞「ところが」specifically mark 逆接 (contrary to expectation), and it is not interchangeable with「〜のに」.
findings.proposed_fix: Either restrict the examples to genuinely adversative cases or note that ～たところ also introduces neutral/expected outcomes.

findings.verbatim: 動て形の「て／で」を「とく」に変えると口語になります。
findings.issue: The colloquial contraction rule is stated incorrectly for で-form verbs: て→とく but で→どく (飲んで→飲んどく, 読んで→読んどく), so instructing learners to change 「で」 to 「とく」 yields the ungrammatical 飲んとく.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The te-form's で is a voiced allomorph after ん/ぐ-stems (飲んで、読んで、急いで), and the colloquial contraction preserves that voicing: 飲んでおく→飲んどく, 読んでおく→読んどく. Instructing learners to replace 「て／で」 with 「とく」 as a single output yields the nonexistent 飲んとく／読んとく; the rule must be stated as て→とく, で→どく. This is not a notational shorthand the learner can recover, since the publisher explicitly lists で as an input but gives only one voiceless output.
findings.correct_fact: The colloquial contraction of ておく is て→とく but で→どく: 掃除しておく→掃除しとく, 飲んでおく→飲んどく, 読んでおく→読んどく (never 飲んとく).
findings.proposed_fix: State that 「て」→「とく」 and 「で」→「どく」.

findings.verbatim: 後件は常に予想される良くない出来事が述べられます。
findings.issue: The contribution asserts that the second clause is *always* an undesirable event, but its own example「いっそ泣けでもしたら楽になれるだろうに、涙は少しも出てくれない。」has a desirable outcome (楽になれる), so the absolute claim contradicts the supplied data.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The pattern ～でもしたら does strongly favor an undesirable consequent, but the explanation's absolute 「常に」 is falsified by the publisher's own eighth example, 「いっそ泣けでもしたら楽になれるだろうに」, where the 後件 is the desirable 楽になれる. In counterfactual ～だろうに / ～ば・たら…のに constructions, ～でもしたら can present a hoped-for but unrealized favorable result; the negativity there attaches to the unstated reality (涙が出ない), not to the consequent clause itself. Teaching 常に therefore misstates the constraint as categorical when it is a strong tendency, and the learner is left unable to parse the very example given.
findings.correct_fact: ～でもしたら usually introduces a hypothetical whose consequence is undesirable, but this is a tendency, not an absolute rule: in counterfactual constructions (…でもしたら～だろうに/のに) the consequent clause can express a desirable outcome that in fact does not occur, e.g. 「いっそ泣けでもしたら楽になれるだろうに」.
findings.proposed_fix: Soften to 'typically an undesirable outcome' and note counterfactual uses with positive consequences.

findings.verbatim: その期間で何らかの大きな変化が生じたことを表す文型です。
findings.issue: 「〜というもの」emphasizes that a state or action continued unbroken throughout a period felt to be long; it does not mean that a big change occurred during that period. The contribution's own example (ずっと荷物の整理をしている) illustrates continuation, not change, so the explanation both misstates the meaning and contradicts its example.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「（ここ／この）＋期間名詞＋というもの」の意味は、話者が長いと感じる期間を取り立てて、その間ずっと同じ状態・動作が途切れず続いたことを強調する用法（例:「この１週間というもの、ずっと荷物の整理をしている」「ここ数年というもの、彼と会っていない」）。「その期間で大きな変化が生じた」という説明は継続・不変の強調という核心をとらえておらず、むしろ逆の内容を述べている。実際、掲載例文の「ずっと〜している」は継続を示しており、説明と例文が整合しない。なお「引っ越してから」という起点表現があるだけで、期間内に変化が起きたことを表す文型ではない。
findings.correct_fact: 「〜というもの」は、長く感じられる一定の期間を取り立て、その間ずっと同じ状態や動作が続いていることを強調する表現であり、その期間中に大きな変化が生じたことを表す文型ではない。
findings.proposed_fix: Restate as 「その期間ずっと同じ状態や動作が続いていることを強調する文型」.

findings.verbatim: すでに起きたことに使います。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that this pattern is used for things that have already happened is contradicted by its own examples, which are hypothetical/future (「どんなに頑張っても１時間以上はかかりそう」 and the general statement 「どんなに負けが続いても応援したくなる」); どんなに〜ても freely covers hypothetical conditions.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「どんなに（いくら）～ても」is a concessive that works equally with realized facts (どんなに探しても見つからなかった) and with unrealized/hypothetical or general-habitual situations (どんなに頑張ってもだめだろう／間に合わないと思う). The only defensible contrast with たとえ～ても is that たとえ is restricted to hypothetical/unrealized cases while どんなに/いくら is NOT so restricted — not that どんなに is limited to past events. The publisher's own examples confirm this: 「どんなに頑張っても１時間以上はかかりそう」is a forward-looking estimate and 「どんなに負けが続いても応援したくなる」is a generic conditional, so the flat statement 「すでに起きたことに使います」would mislead a learner into avoiding a fully standard use.
findings.correct_fact: どんなに（いくら）～ても is not limited to events that have already occurred; it covers realized facts, general/habitual statements, and hypothetical or future conditions alike. Only たとえ～ても carries the restriction to unrealized/hypothetical situations.
findings.proposed_fix: State only that たとえ〜ても is restricted to not-yet-realised situations, without claiming どんなに〜ても is limited to already-occurred ones.

findings.verbatim: 前件と後件の主語は同一でなければいけません。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that the subjects of the preceding and following clauses must be identical is contradicted by this contribution's own examples, e.g. 小学生が作ったにしてはクオリティが高すぎる (subject 小学生 vs クオリティ) and ここの家賃は、駅に近いにしてはあまり高くない.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: Taken literally, 「前件と後件の主語は同一でなければいけません」 is false: にしては only requires that the 前件 supply a standard/attribute pertaining to the same topic being evaluated, not that the two clauses share a grammatical subject. The entry's own examples prove this — in 「小学生が作ったにしてはクオリティが高すぎる」 the 前件 subject is 小学生 while the 後件 subject is クオリティ, and in 「ここの家賃は、駅に近いにしてはあまり高くない」 the 前件 predicate 近い takes ここ(物件) as its subject while the 後件 subject is 家賃 (a whole–part/possession relation, not identity). A charitable reading as 同一主体/同一主題 would be defensible, but as written with 主語 and the absolute なければいけません it would lead a learner to reject perfectly natural sentences such as 「田中さんが作ったにしては、この料理はまずい」.
findings.correct_fact: にしては does not require identical grammatical subjects in the two clauses; it requires that the 前件 give a standard or property relating to the same entity/topic being evaluated in the 後件 (hence 小学生が作ったにしてはクオリティが高すぎる, 駅に近いにしては家賃は高くない are both correct).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop or heavily qualify the same-subject requirement, since にしては readily takes a standard-setting phrase unrelated to the main subject.

findings.verbatim: 良くないことに対してのみ用いられます。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that this pattern is used only for undesirable matters is too strong and is contradicted by several of the contribution's own examples, which are neutral or positive (e.g. 「運動に限ったことではないが、何事も繰り返してこそ上達するものだ。」 and 「礼儀が必要なのは社会人だけに限ったことではない。」).
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「〜に限らない／〜に限ったことではない」is a purely logical negation of exclusivity (「Xだけではない」) and is freely used with neutral and desirable content; the negative-topic bias is at most a statistical tendency of 「〜に限ったことではない」when it introduces a complaint, never a restriction. The publisher's own examples disprove the 「のみ」claim: 「運動に限ったことではないが、何事も繰り返してこそ上達するものだ」and 「礼儀が必要なのは社会人だけに限ったことではない」involve improvement and politeness, and 「契約は身近な所にたくさんある。ビジネスに限ったことではない」is neutral. A learner told the form is licensed only for 良くないこと would wrongly reject the very sentences presented as models.
findings.correct_fact: 〜に限らない／〜に限ったことではない simply denies that something is limited to the named case; it can be used with negative, neutral, or positive content (e.g. 礼儀が必要なのは社会人に限らない). Only a mild tendency toward complaint-like contexts exists with 〜に限ったことではない, not an absolute restriction.
findings.proposed_fix: Soften to note that ～に限ったことではない often (but not exclusively) refers to undesirable situations.

findings.verbatim: 過去のことにしか使えません。
findings.issue: The claim that ものだから can only be used for past events is incorrect and is contradicted by this contribution's own examples, several of which have non-past clauses (e.g. ずっと座ってるもんだからお尻が痛い。/ 一人暮らしが長いもんだから料理も自然と上達する。). ものだから freely takes non-past predicates in both clauses.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: ものだから requires only that the consequence be a realized/factual state, not that it be past-tense; non-past predicates in both clauses are entirely normal (e.g. 忙しいものだから、なかなか行けません／子どもが小さいものだから、夜は出られない). The contribution's own examples (お尻が痛い、料理も自然と上達する、人前で思いっきり笑いたくない、うるさい) are all non-past, so the flat statement 過去のことにしか使えません is self-contradicting and would mislead a learner. The genuine restriction usually taught is that the main clause cannot be a command, request, invitation or volitional expression (×うるさいものだから、静かにしてください), which is a different constraint from tense.
findings.correct_fact: ものだから/もんだから can take non-past predicates in both the reason clause and the result clause; the real restriction is that the result clause must state a fact/state, not an imperative, request, invitation or volitional expression.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete or restrict this claim; ものだから is not limited to past reference.

findings.verbatim: 「～よう」は他動詞のます形に接続して方法を表すので
findings.issue: The explanation states the pattern attaches only to transitive verbs (他動詞), but the contribution's own examples include intransitive verbs, e.g. 「直接言ってくれないことには分かりようがない。」and「人柄の良さなんて、初対面では実際分かりようもない。」(分かる is intransitive). The restriction is both too narrow and contradicted internally.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「分かる」は辞書・学校文法いずれでも自動詞(自五)であり(「日本語が分かる」のガ格は主語扱い)、他にも「逃げようがない」「なりようがない」など自動詞に付く例は普通に成立する。したがって「他動詞のます形に接続」という限定は誤りで、実質的な制約は他動性ではなく意志性(意志動詞であること)である。しかも当該投稿自身が「分かりようがない/分かりようもない」を例示しており、説明と例が内部矛盾している。
findings.correct_fact: 「～ようがない」は他動詞に限らず動詞のます形一般(特に意志動詞。自動詞の「逃げる・なる」等も可)に接続し、「分かりようがない」のように自動詞にも付く。制約があるとすれば他動性ではなく意志性である。
findings.proposed_fix: Drop 「他動詞の」 and say it attaches to the ます形 of volitional/action verbs generally.

findings.verbatim: 一般常識や規則、経験などに基づいた主観的判断により物事を行わなければならないことを表します。
findings.issue: Polarity mismatch: the plain 動辞形＋わけにはいかない form listed in the same contribution's structure means "cannot / must not do", yet the explanation states only that the pattern expresses 〜しなければならない (obligation to do), which properly describes 〜ないわけにはいかない; most of the examples (負けるわけにはいかない, 死ぬわけにはいかない, 迷惑をかけるわけにはいかない) mean the opposite of what is explained.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The core meaning of 動辞形＋わけにはいかない is 「〜することはできない／してはいけない」— impossibility or prohibition arising from social norms, circumstances or one's own principles (e.g. 負けるわけにはいかない = 'we cannot afford to lose'). The explanation as written, 「…物事を行わなければならないことを表します」, states positive obligation to perform the very action named by the verb, which is the meaning of the negative-stem variant 〜ないわけにはいかない (助けないわけにはいかない = 'I have to help'). Although one could strain to read 「物事を行う」 as generic 'to act in accordance with one's judgment', the natural reading directly contradicts six of the eight cited examples, and the entry never states the 'cannot/must not' sense at all, so a learner would be misinformed about polarity.
findings.correct_fact: V(辞書形)＋わけにはいかない means 'cannot / must not do V' (impossibility or prohibition for social, moral or circumstantial reasons); only V(ない形)＋ないわけにはいかない expresses the obligation 'have to do V'.
findings.proposed_fix: State that 動辞形＋わけにはいかない means "cannot/must not do" and that only the ない形 version expresses obligation.

findings.verbatim: 人物や地域を表す名詞に接続し
findings.issue: The stated restriction (attaches only to nouns denoting people or regions) is both incorrect for this pattern and contradicted by the contribution's own examples, which attach it to 今 (time), 恋, and 教育.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 「Nをおいて他にない」 places no lexical restriction on N beyond it being a noun phrase whose referent is being singled out; standard references note it is *frequently* used with person nouns but freely admits things, times, places, and abstract nouns (今をおいてほかにない、これをおいてほかに方法はない). Stating flatly that it 「人物や地域を表す名詞に接続し」 turns a frequency tendency into a grammatical constraint, and the publisher's own examples (今、恋、教育、大学) violate it in five of eight sentences, so a learner would wrongly conclude such uses are ungrammatical. 「地域」 is also a needlessly narrow substitute for 「場所」/「もの」.
findings.correct_fact: をおいて他にない attaches to any noun (people, places, times, things, abstract concepts) meaning 「～以外にない・～だけだ」; person nouns are merely the most common case, not a requirement.
findings.proposed_fix: State that it attaches to nouns generally (people, places, times, things), rather than restricting it to persons and regions.

findings.verbatim: 「始める」は他動詞なので、自分の意志による動作につきます。
findings.issue: The stated restriction to volitional actions is contradicted by the contribution's own material: 「髪の毛が抜け始めた。」 and the note's 「雨が降り始める」 are non-volitional events, and V-masu+始める freely attaches to natural phenomena.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: As a compound-verb suffix, 〜始める attaches freely to both volitional and non-volitional predicates: 雨が降り始める, 桜が咲き始める, 髪が抜け始める, 日が暮れ始める are all standard, and the contribution itself supplies two such non-volitional examples. Moreover the paired claim is worse than merely over-restrictive: there is no productive 動ます形＋始まる compound in modern Japanese (×降り始まる, ×咲き始まる), so the transitive/intransitive contrast the explanation invokes cannot do the work assigned to it — the real transitive/intransitive alternation belongs to the independent verbs (〜を始める／〜が始まる), not to the V-masu compound. The only defensible core is that 他動詞 始める requires an agent when used independently, which does not license the stated restriction on the compound.
findings.correct_fact: V-masu＋始める marks the onset of any process, volitional or not (雨が降り始める, 髪が抜け始める); 始まる does not form V-masu compounds at all (×降り始まる). The volitional/non-volitional and transitive/intransitive contrast applies only to independent 〜を始める vs 〜が始まる, and the real nuance contrast for compounds is 〜始める (gradual) vs 〜出す (sudden).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the volitional-only restriction and note that ～始める attaches to both volitional actions and spontaneous phenomena.

findings.verbatim: 後項に接続できるのは意志動詞のみです。
findings.issue: The stated restriction that only volitional verbs can appear in the main clause is incorrect for ～た後で／後に, and it is contradicted by the contribution's own examples (「必ずお腹が痛くなる」「忘れ物をしたことに気づいた」are non-volitional).
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: There is no volitional-verb restriction on the main clause of 〜た後で／後に; unlike 〜次第 or 〜てからでないと (where 後件 must be an intentional act), 〜た後 freely takes non-volitional predicates: 「地震が起きた後で津波が来た」「食べた後で気分が悪くなった」. The publisher's own examples prove it — 「必ずお腹が痛くなる」(spontaneous 変化動詞) and 「忘れ物をしたことに気づいた」(無意志動詞 気づく) — so the rule as stated is not a defensible alternative analysis but a mis-transplanted restriction, and a learner would wrongly reject perfectly natural sentences.
findings.correct_fact: 〜た後で／後に places no restriction on the main-clause verb: non-volitional/spontaneous predicates (なる、気づく、痛くなる、来る etc.) are fully acceptable. The 'main clause must be a volitional verb' constraint belongs to other patterns such as 〜次第 or 〜てからでないと〜ない.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete or soften the volitional-verb restriction, which applies (partially) to ～てから rather than ～た後で.

findings.verbatim: 場所を表す名詞につくと、物理的位置関係の前方を表します。
findings.issue: With place nouns 後 indicates the space *behind* (後方／うしろ), not 前方 ('in front / forward'); the direction is stated backwards, which misinforms about the meaning.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: 後 attached to a place noun denotes the region 後方／うしろ (behind), never 前方 (in front); e.g. 家の後(ろ)＝behind the house. The publisher's own following sentence (その場合「～後ろ（うしろ）」となることが多いです) contradicts 前方, showing the direction word is simply reversed — likely copied from the 前に entry. Unlike the temporal line, where '前方' could conceivably be stretched to mean 'ahead on the timeline', for physical space 前方 unambiguously means the front side, so a learner is misinformed.
findings.correct_fact: When 後 follows a place noun it indicates the space behind (後方／うしろ), e.g. 建物の後ろ = behind the building; it does not indicate 前方 ('in front').
findings.proposed_fix: Change 前方 to 後方 in the spatial description.

findings.verbatim: 人の行動や動作に関係する他動詞のます形にのみ接続でき
findings.issue: The stated restriction to transitive verbs only is too strong and is contradicted within the same contribution: 住む is listed among the acceptable verbs (「言う、読む、書く、住む、作る、見る、する、やる」) and 住み慣れた appears as the first example, yet 住む is intransitive; likewise 通い慣れた (also intransitive) is admitted as an exception. Other intransitive combinations such as 歩き慣れた道 or 行き慣れた店 are also normal.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: The real constraint on ～慣れる is that the V-masu stem be a controllable/volitional verb (意志動詞), not that it be transitive: 歩き慣れた道、行き慣れた店、座り慣れた椅子、通い慣れた道、住み慣れた町 are all fully natural with intransitive verbs. The publisher's own list includes 住む, which is unambiguously 自動詞 (東京に住む, never *東京を住む), and their sole escape hatch — 移動系の動詞 as an exception — does not cover 住む, so the 他動詞のみ claim is internally contradicted, not merely simplified. The contrast they actually want is with non-volitional/uncontrollable verbs (降る、吹く、疲れる), which is a volitionality distinction, not a transitivity one.
findings.correct_fact: ～慣れる attaches to the masu-stem of volitional (controllable) verbs, whether transitive or intransitive: 住み慣れる、通い慣れる、歩き慣れる、行き慣れる、座り慣れる are all correct; the true exclusion is non-volitional verbs such as 降る、吹く、疲れる.
findings.proposed_fix: Restate the rule as attaching to the masu-stem of volitional/controllable verbs (both transitive and intransitive) rather than 他動詞 only.

findings.verbatim: 「食事の最中」と言えば、食事をしている時の最も楽しい時を指します。
findings.issue: 「食事の最中」simply means "in the middle of eating / while the meal is going on"; it does not designate the "most enjoyable moment" of the meal. Defining 最中 as the emotionally peak/most-fun point misstates the meaning of the pattern.
findings.second_opinion_reasoning: Dictionaries gloss 最中 as 「物事がいちばん盛んに行われているとき／ちょうど…しているとき」— i.e. the temporal midst or height of an ongoing event, with no component of enjoyment or emotional climax. 「食事の最中に電話が鳴った」means simply 'the phone rang while I was eating', not 'at the most enjoyable point of the meal'; likewise the publisher's own examples 「帰宅の最中」「調査を行っている最中」「寝ている最中」have no 'peak of fun' at all, so the gloss contradicts its own data. The derived claim that 「水を飲んでいる最中」is impossible because drinking water lacks an exciting phase is also unsupported — such sentences (水を飲んでいる最中にむせた) occur naturally; the real constraint is that the predicate denote a durative activity.
findings.correct_fact: 最中 marks the middle/course of an ongoing action or state ('in the midst of, while ~ is going on'). 「食事の最中」means 'while (someone is) eating / in the middle of the meal', not 'the most enjoyable moment of the meal'; 最中 carries no meaning of emotional peak or fun.
findings.proposed_fix: State that 最中 marks the midst/height of an ongoing action or event, without implying it is the most enjoyable moment.
